prompt.context: Your client is a major pharmaceutical company who has recently acquired a small biotech company. They have asked you to advise them on the merger, the structure of its sales force, and the potential risks going forward. The CEO is coming to meet with us in about 30 minutes and would like to have a recommendation.
prompt.question: Please walk through your thought process on how you would advise the client on: (1) the implications of the merger, (2) how to maximize strengths and minimize risks, and (3) what recommendation you would make to the CEO.

clarifying_info.q: Where is the large pharmaceutical company headquartered?
clarifying_info.a: Headquartered in the Northeast United States.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the large pharma company currently sell?
clarifying_info.a: Currently sells cardiovascular, diabetes, and oncology drugs, and is developing additional drugs in those therapeutic areas. It has a large, experienced sales force.

clarifying_info.q: What does the small biotech company sell or have in the pipeline?
clarifying_info.a: Located in California. One autoimmune drug was approved by the FDA last year; two more drugs are in early stages of development. It has a small, inexperienced sales force.

clarifying_info.q: Are any numbers available for this analysis?
clarifying_info.a: No numbers will be provided for this case. Please make reasonable assumptions.

framework: Corporate considerations: human resources, profitability (new and old business, expenses), efficiencies or lack thereof, physical location of employees, manufacturing facilities

Sales force considerations: experienced vs. inexperienced reps, geographic location (Northeast vs. California), impact on customers (physicians, payers, patients), current product mix each rep sells, how the sales force should be organized going forward

Risks: bi-coastal merger inefficiencies, high relocation costs, employee turnover, PR implications, regulatory risks (drug development and drug sales), supply chain issues, sub-optimal sales force structure

questions.prompt: What are the key corporate implications of this merger?
questions.guidance: Candidate should discuss HR integration (managing two workforces across coasts), profitability and cost structure of both entities, potential synergies and inefficiencies, physical location and whether to consolidate, and manufacturing/supply chain alignment. No numbers required; credit structured reasoning and logical assumptions.

questions.prompt: How can the client maximize the strengths of the merger and minimize its risks?
questions.guidance: Strengths to maximize: access to a new autoimmune drug and pipeline, expanded therapeutic coverage, potential cross-selling or bundling. Risks to minimize: clearly communicate integration plan to reduce turnover, establish a relocation or remote-work policy to manage bi-coastal challenges, ensure regulatory compliance processes are harmonized, plan for sales force structure early (e.g., separate specialty vs. primary care reps, or integrate). Interviewer should push back to test poise and ability to defend reasoning.

questions.prompt: What is your recommendation to the CEO?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will provide a clear, structured C-level recommendation covering: (1) integrate sales forces carefully given geographic and experience gap — consider keeping a dedicated specialty biotech team in California for the autoimmune product while leveraging the established pharma reps for existing products; (2) prioritize culture and HR integration to reduce turnover risk; (3) align on regulatory and supply chain processes early; (4) set a clear timeline and ownership for each integration workstream. Excellent candidates show comfort with ambiguity (no numbers), maintain poise under pushback, and add original insight.

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the risks the client should be aware of going forward with this merger?

categories.name: Operational / Efficiency
ideas: Different corporate cultures may slow integration
Manufacturing facilities may be duplicative or incompatible

categories.name: Human Resources
ideas: High employee turnover during and after merger
Retaining top biotech talent accustomed to startup culture
Experienced pharma reps unfamiliar with autoimmune products

categories.name: Sales Force Structure
ideas: Sub-optimal sales force structure if not redesigned
Geographic coverage gaps if California biotech reps are not retained
Mixed product portfolios may confuse reps or physicians
Impact on customer (physician, payer, patient) relationships

categories.name: Regulatory / Legal
ideas: Ongoing drug development risk for two early-stage drugs
Drug sales compliance obligations differ by therapeutic area

categories.name: Financial / Strategic
ideas: Integration costs may offset near-term synergies
New autoimmune category may require new market access strategy
Pipeline drugs may fail in later clinical stages

recommendation: Proceed with the merger but implement a phased integration: retain the California biotech team as a dedicated autoimmune specialty unit in the near term, while leveraging the existing Northeast pharma sales force for cardiovascular, diabetes, and oncology

Redesign the combined sales force structure around therapeutic areas rather than legacy company lines, with clear role definitions and territory planning to serve physicians, payers, and patients optimally
risks: Bi-coastal operations increase coordination costs and slow decision-making
Employee turnover — particularly of specialized biotech talent — could erode the value of the acquired pipeline
Regulatory and supply chain differences between the two entities could cause compliance issues if not harmonized early
next_steps: Conduct a full HR and organizational audit to identify overlap and gaps across both workforces
Establish a cross-functional integration task force with clear milestones and ownership
Define the long-term sales force structure (specialty vs. primary care, geographic footprint) within 90 days
Initiate regulatory harmonization review for drug development and sales compliance across all therapeutic areas
